scientific_basis: Measures native-waveform plateau morphology compatible with hard clipping or saturation; not the full nonlinear-distortion construct.
All three outputs reconstruct from accepted-plateau and merged-episode ledgers for 519 recordings.
Native-rate PCM, native channels, task span, complete frames, hashes, and immutable v3.1.1 baseline are verified.
Polarity, aligned translation, attenuation after clipping, and lossless PCM behave as specified; resampling/lossy coding can erase plateaus.
Controlled hard-clipping burden yields ordered frame/sample response and perfect precision; recall is conservative at smallest doses.
Clean speech, natural extrema, quantization, impulses/noise and moderate smooth saturation are not promoted; causal clipping stage is not identifiable.
All 519 are available; Poisson intervals, merge-gap sensitivity, threshold margins and delete-one influence are retained because only 15 episodes occur.
Negative agreement is high, positive agreement is 0.40, and positive-part magnitude reliability is not estimable.
All accepted, rejected and valid-zero items were reviewed label-blind; adjudication is AI-assisted and 13 rejected items remain ambiguous.
No scalar, standalone gate, imputation, complete-distortion claim or independent-view claim is authorized.
